solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: cooking something changes its make-up, so the letters of crumpets are mixed up

explanation.surface: A kitchen range is just the thing for toasting a batch of crumpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like the cooker on which the crumpets are cooked, but it is the definition in its other sense: a full span.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full sweep of values or colours, so it is a synonym for a range.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to peer is to look hard, trying to make something out
second meaning: ... of the realm are members of the nobility

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a verb of squinting and a plural noun for lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who peers strains their eyes to make something out; peers are also dukes, earls and other titled nobility.

clue.text: Explain trophy inscribed with name of tragic king

indicators.note: a name engraved on a cup sits within it, so the king's name goes inside the trophy

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an explanation of why a trophy is engraved with a doomed monarch's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a puzzle or confusion is to explain it, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Sailor turning up is unpleasant person

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tar (Jack Tar) is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who shows up turns out to be a nasty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads as arriving; in a down entry it means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a rat is calling them a contemptible, treacherous person.

clue.text: Sort of preacher to want more liars converted

indicators.note: something converted is changed into a new form, so the letters of more liars are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of preacher longs to see more liars converted to honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' fits the preacher's world of saving souls, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A moraliser lectures others on right and wrong, which is one kind of preaching.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... fastens a door or box
second meaning: a tress or curl of hair

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a hair clip, but it is two separate meanings joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock secures a door shut, and a lock of hair is a single tress.

indicators.note: made different, the five letters of Melon are put in another order

explanation.surface: A melon is quite a different fruit from the one you might expect.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit.

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like My!
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Someone's face is glowing with warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, the same as 'My!', which is why 'My' gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial manner is friendly and warm, giving off warmth towards others.

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery and ties
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A pet parrot is handed some cloth to chew on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is the bird in the surface, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot words is to echo them mechanically, which is to say them again.

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letter headings
Mark's gospel follows Matthew's in the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone passes comment on who followed Matthew.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written observation, the same thing as a comment.

indicators.note: something protected is shielded inside, so the answer lies within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A monarch is guarded by aides as they arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, a supreme ruler.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wickedness can disturb a whole city.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a large port city on Spain's eastern coast.

clue.text: Saint opposing a time of fasting in East

parts.note: V is short for versus, meaning against or opposing
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A saint stands against a period of fasting in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: St Valentine is the martyr whose feast day on 14 February is celebrated by lovers.

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a pal is a chum, a friend

explanation.surface: Someone startles a friend who is usually silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to horrify or dismay them, a strong synonym for shock.

clue.text: Very impressive ace, first person to get total read out

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: read out means spoken aloud, so the words are judged by sound, not spelling

parts.note: we is the first person plural pronoun, and a sum is a total, so this gives WE SUM

explanation.surface: A card player announces a staggering total score.
explanation.walkthrough: WE SUM said aloud sounds like WESOME; A for the ace goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awesome inspires awe, so it is extremely impressive.

clue.text: Fibre shown by little girl confronting gangster?

parts.note: sis is a short, familiar word for a sister
Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A small girl shows fibre by standing up to a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'gangster' stands for one particular gangster's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fork-tailed migrating bird
second meaning: to ... food is to get it down

explanation.walkthrough: 'get down' sounds like descending, but it means swallowing food.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a small migrant songbird, and to swallow is to send food down the throat.

parts.note: to beg is to request earnestly
inner means private or intimate, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A close friend makes a plea on behalf of a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is a novice just starting out, which is what a learner is.

clue.text: I had a small house somewhere in America

parts.note: 'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd
ho is the abbreviation for house, so small house is the short form

explanation.surface: Someone recalls owning a little house somewhere in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' does not mean a cottage: it signals the shortened form of house.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States, so it is a place in America.

clue.text: A record with minimum of snow in the mountains

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

indicators.note: the least possible amount of snow is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A recording made with hardly any snow on the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are Europe's best-known mountain range, often called simply the mountains.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to don clothes is to put them on
second meaning: to stage a play is to put it on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Don's' reads as belonging to a man called Don, but it is 'Don is': each word is a meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: You put on a coat when you dress, and a theatre company puts on a show when it presents it.

clue.text: Thus African country must be African!

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a certain country must surely be in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'African' is the definition: a person from Somalia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a native of Somalia in the Horn of Africa, so is an African.

indicators.note: one who drinks takes the drink inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
It is Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and It

explanation.surface: A well-mannered European sips a vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for Italian vermouth is a British bar term, from the cocktail gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite behaviour is courteous and well-mannered, the conduct of a civilised person.

clue.text: Provincial party set up — food provided

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so it reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the DUP (Democratic Unionist Party) is a party in Northern Ireland, known as the Province

explanation.surface: A regional political party organises a meal for supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called 'the Province' in Britain, hence the Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert, so it is a kind of food.

indicators.note: turned around, the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone orders the editor about, in a protesting mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for demonstration, a public rally of protest.

clue.text: Providing funds for the last bit unpaid

parts.note: the end is the last bit of something
money owing is still unpaid

explanation.surface: Someone funds the final portion of a bill not yet settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow a college or hospital is to give it a lasting income, so endowing is financing it.
